hero.title: ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING POST GRADUATION IN FRANCE
hero.subtitle: **Studying Postgraduate (PG) Electrical Engineering in France** is a great opportunity for students who want to gain advanced technical knowledge and professional skills in electrical power systems, renewable energy, automation, electronics, smart grids, and industrial control. The French universities and engineering schools offer specialized master’s programs combining theory, lab work, research projects and industry experience.

overview: **Studying Postgraduate (PG) Electrical Engineering in France** is a great opportunity for students who want to gain advanced technical knowledge and professional skills in electrical power systems, renewable energy, automation, electronics, smart grids, and industrial control. The French universities and engineering schools offer specialized master’s programs combining theory, lab work, research projects and industry experience.

France is a popular destination for students wanting to study a ****Master’s in Electrical Engineering in France**** because of its advanced electricity networks, energy efficiency initiatives, electric mobility and intelligent industrial systems. International students will be able to choose from selected **English-taught master’s programs in France** or French-taught pathways depending on their academic background and career ambitions.

Students can explore suitable ****Electrical Engineering courses in France****, understand the admission requirements and prepare for their study abroad journey with ****Edu Hawk worldwide study abroad guidance**.**

sections.title: 1. How long is a postgraduate electrical engineering course in France?

items: In France, a national **Master's degree in Electrical Engineering** usually corresponds to a two-year course (M1 and M2) for a total of 120 ECTS credits. Some programs and engineering qualifications have different structures.

sections.title: 2. Can Indian students do Electrical Engineering PG in France?

items: Yes **Indian students can study postgraduate Electrical Engineering in France** if they meet the academic, language and documentation criteria. University admission and student-visa approval are two different processes.

sections.title: 3. Is IELTS required for electrical engineering in masters in France?

items: Not always. **French master’s programs taught in English** may accept IELTS, TOEFL, another approved language test or evidence of previous English-medium education where permitted. Some taught programs in French may require you to have knowledge of French.

sections.title: 4. What is the tuition fee for PG in Electrical Engineering in France?

items: For 2026-2027, the reference fee for a national master’s degree in the covered public institutions is €255 per year for EU/EEA/Swiss students and €3,950 for non-EU students subject to differentiated fees. Special programs and exemptions may alter the amount payable.

sections.title: 5. What are the career prospects after PG in Electrical Engineering in France?

items: Graduates can find jobs in **electrical design, power systems, renewable energy, power electronics, automation, smart grids, embedded systems, and research and development.** Opportunities depend on technical expertise, experience, language ability and employer requirements.

sections.title: 6. Is it possible to study Electrical Engineering in France in English?

items: Yes. **Electrical Engineering master’s programs in English** (including specialized programs in smart grids and energy systems) are offered in selected French universities and engineering institutions. Students should check the language of instruction and language requirements for each program.

Students must verify the exact qualification awarded before accepting an offer for a ****postgraduate Electrical Engineering program in France**.**

A French **diplôme national de master** is an officially recognized qualification in the French higher education system and in the European higher education area. It generally means five years of study beyond the secondary level when added to the previous bachelor-level study.
Check before you sign up:
- The official title of the degree.
- If the program leads to a national master degree or an engineering diploma.
- The status of recognition or accreditation of the institution.
- The academic credits and length.
- Recognition requirements for further education or employment in your destination country.
Students who are planning to return to India should consult prospective employers, universities or relevant authorities to determine qualification and employment requirements.

**Salary in Electrical Engineering in France**

There is no average salary for all **Electrical Engineering graduates in France**. Salary will vary depending on the position, the location, the company, your prior experience, your language skills and whether it is an internship or a permanent job.

Applicants are to compare current job advertisements and salary surveys for their preferred specialization. When looking over an offer they should also consider taxes and social contributions, accommodation and other living expenses.

sections.title: 10. Required documents for Electrical Engineering PG in France**

items: Students applying for ****Electrical Engineering postgraduate courses in France**** generally need the following documents:
- A valid passport.
- Bachelor’s degree certificate or provisional degree certificate.
- Transcripts (official)
- CV or résumé.
- Motivation Letter (Statement of Purpose).
- Letters of recommendation, if required.
- English language test results, where applicable.
- Certificate in French, as appropriate.
- Course Syllabus or descriptions available upon request.
- Details of applicable technical projects and internships.
- Certificates of experience or employment, if any.
- Passport size photographs, if needed.
- Confirmation of application fee (where applicable).

Some universities may require certified translations in English or French. ****Applications for a French student visa**** often require additional documents, such as proof of funds and accommodation where appropriate.
